current.text: He re-signed with the Thunder on a 3-year, 75 million USD contract.
Experts expect him to be the full-time starting center, and they see his role as secure.
The other OKC bigs are Chet Holmgren, Al Horford, Jaylin Williams and Thomas Sorber. Jaylin Williams barely played unless the centers were out.
He was banged up a lot last season. He was playing very well early in the season before he got hurt.
Experts say he goes too late in drafts. They think he should go inside the top 100, but on ESPN he sits outside the top 130.
If he stays healthy and plays 28 to 29 minutes, he is a top 60 player. One expert gives a best case of 40th and a worst case of 93rd.
In mock drafts, experts took him around round 8 for his defensive stats. In a 12-team mock, he went around pick 116.

durable.text: He is a center who gets assists at a rate that is unusual for his position.
He gives rebounds, steals, blocks and a high FG% on top of his assists.

note: The market has him near the cutoff of our 144-player draft: Yahoo rank 103 (average cost 1.2 USD) and ESPN rank 135 (0.5 USD). Experts see top 100 value and top 60 upside at 28 or more minutes, so he is a cheap end-game target. Our league paid 11 USD for him last season, so a few USD is a better price. He fits punt 3PM builds and gives rebounds, assists, steals and a 61% FG%. His 64% FT% comes on only about 2 attempts per game, so the damage there is small. Early in the season, check that he is healthy and playing close to 28 minutes, up from 24.3 last season.
